channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Lear opens first office outside of Italy
item.description: Italian economic consultancy Lear has hired the former chief economist at Portugal's Competition Authority to co-head its newly established Lisbon office.

item.title: Assefi asks staff to “empty the clip”
item.description: The Department of Justice’s antitrust division has been far too timid in bringing civil enforcement actions, the acting head of the agency has said, challenging staff to “keep up with the pace we have set in the criminal programme”.

item.title: Hard reset: The Tipline for 17 February 2026
item.description: Paramount is hoping this reboot fares better than Frasier 2.0. Warner Bros Discovery has given Paramount one week to improve its offer ahead of a 20 March shareholder meeting to seek approval for Netflix’s offer. Warner Bros chief executive David Zaslav said he had given Paramount “clear direction on the deficiencies in their offers and opportunities to address them”. Also in Tipline, Makan Delrah...

item.title: States accuse DOJ of withholding “substantial” HPE docs
item.description: The Colorado-led state challengers to the Hewlett Packard Enterprises/Juniper Networks approval have claimed the Department of Justice is stonewalling their bid to obtain crucial evidence about the controversial settlement.

item.title: All ears: The Briefing for 18 February 2026
item.description: The European Commission could yet face pushback against its decision to conditionally clear UMG’s takeover of Downtown. IMPALA, a vocal critic of the deal, said today it is waiting to learn more about the watchdog’s full reasoning before considering a potential challenge. Also in The Briefing, Sanofi names CSL Seqirus as the complainant in the commission’s disparagement probe.

item.title: Complainants target CMA’s enforcement record in growth consultation
item.description: The UK competition watchdog’s “failure” to “intervene early and decisively” against the world’s most powerful tech companies is causing an increasing reliance on private damages claims and shifting enforcement from “prevention to compensation”, a complainant group has warned.

item.title: Denmark launches first below-threshold in-depth probe
item.description: Denmark’s Competition and Consumer Authority has launched its first in-depth probe into a below-threshold deal, investigating Uber’s already-completed acquisition of the country’s largest taxi company.

item.title: Merchants suffered majority of interchange fee losses, CAT says in landmark ruling
item.description: Visa and Mastercard have largely failed to prove that retailers passed on the overcharges from their multilateral interchange fees to consumers, the UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal has said in a ruling expected to have wide-ranging ramifications for several ongoing claims.

item.title: FTC appeals against HSR rule defeat
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission has asked the US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit to overturn a lower court’s ruling finding it failed to justify its expansion of merging filing requirements.

item.title: Facing the music: The Tipline for 18 February 2026
item.description: The Department of Justice is still scheduled to perform its Live Nation show next month, just expect a shorter set list. On Wednesday, the US District Court for the Southern District of New York granted Live Nation’s request to trim allegations that it cornered competition for promotion services and fan ticket sales at major concert venues.
